primitives.name: Few-Shot Identity Bootstrapping
primitives.verbatim_quote: **Verdict:** ADAPT — an offline, annotation-efficient player-tracking system that learns game-specific identities from ~6 short tracklet annotations per player (incremental Transformer-based ReID), beating ByteTrack by +26 pp IDF1 on rugby sevens and releasing a public moving-camera tracking dataset.

primitives.assumptions: Players are distinguishable by appearance and motion within short tracklets; annotations are temporally consistent.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When tracklet length < l_min=10 frames or IoU threshold μ < 0.5, identity ambiguity increases.

primitives.verbatim_quote: Method / model - **Tracklet generation (§3.2):** Faster R-CNN ResNet-50 (COCO-trained) detects persons; SORT-style IoU bipartite matching + Kalman filter links boxes; tracklets intersecting with IoU > μ=0.5 are split (treated as ambiguous); tracklets shorter than l_min=10 frames discarded → "non-ambiguous" single-identity tracklets.

primitives.verbatim_quote: bag-of-tricks ResNet-50 ReID (Market1501-pretrained; 256×128 input, d_1=2048) → FC to d_2=128 → Transformer (16 encoder layers, 1 decoder layer, 16 heads; N_q=32 learned DETR-style queries, no positional encoding since tracklets resampled to d_t=10 frames; top N_qc=4 queries backpropagated) → batch norm → tracklet fe

primitives.assumptions: Appearance features are sufficient for distinguishing players; transformer learns identity-specific representations.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When N_qc < 4 or query attention fails, identity confusion arises.

reasoning_traces.think:
ADAPT's framework integrates two core components: tracklet generation and incremental ReID. Tracklets are generated using Faster R-CNN and SORT-style matching, producing temporally coherent sequences of bounding boxes. These are then processed through a ResNet-50-based ReID module, followed by a Transformer that learns identity-specific embeddings. The key innovation lies in few-shot learning where only ~6 tracklets per player are required to bootstrap identity assignments. This enables robust tracking even in challenging environments such as rugby sevens with high motion, occlusion, and similar kit appearances. The system uses a dual-training regime: frozen ResNet for interactive annotation and fine-tuned version for final performance. Association is done via either iterative greedy selection or RNMF, balancing completeness and identity purity. The method addresses the fundamental challenge of generic MOT/ReID failing on team sports due to their unique visual and kinematic properties.
